lessons.lesson: Before finalizing, tally each day's per-person cost from grounded prices and swap or drop stops until every day stays under the budget cap.
Order searches broad-to-specific: major landmarks first, then food/lodging/accessibility needs, then outlying sites, so later queries refine grounded candidates.

When a named-place query returns 0 results, retry a few broader or alternate forms (drop the qualifier, local-language name, transliteration), then stop and pivot to grounded substitutes the tool does return instead of re-running the same empty query.
Before writing the itinerary, verify each stop's exact name matches a returned POI record, not just a name in a results list, and replace unverified stops with grounded alternatives.
Only call calculate_distance with POI ids a prior search returned; if a call fails with an unknown POI id, re-search that place and retry the distance before moving on.
After selecting grounded stops, call calculate_distance on the chosen pairs to validate and order each day's route before writing the final itinerary.
When a special need (pet, accessibility) is requested, run a dedicated query for it and only include places that query returned; if it returns nothing, retry with alternate wording before finalizing.
When a category query returns off-target name-matched venues, retry with a more specific compound phrase before trusting those results as grounded.
